title: Grateful Dead Live at Ungano's Night Club on 1970-02-12
taper: Any/all editing, fades, NR, hiss elimination, phase shifting/"time smear" correction, jitter elimination, and +/-2 dB max. EQ were performed using 100% digital-only processing (24-bit/96 kHz data stream) at Serafin Station Studio B
source: SBD > 2-track RTR @ 15 i.p.s. > PCM > ? > D > SSSB

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear soundboard tape with strong playing – highlights include Black Peter and Saint Stephen, though the show is considered only average by some.
ai_review.review: The recording is praised for its crystal‑clear, almost pristine sound quality, typical of a soundboard source. Musically the performance is solid, delivering a nice Black Peter and a good Saint Stephen, but several listeners note that it isn’t an especially historic or standout show overall.

ai_rating.rationale: Three reviewers rate the audio and playing highly (5‑star comments) while one warns not to expect a great show; overall the combination of good soundboard quality and decent but unremarkable performance yields a solid above‑average rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Multiple reviewers describe the tape as "crystal" and "sounds great," noting clear instrument separation and a vivid crowd roar at the end of Casey Jones. No significant drop‑outs or muffling reported.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Early‑1970 show with a mix of familiar material; while the playing is good, reviewers feel it lacks the excitement of later shows.
